Maya (People Ops): @channel quick heads-up — today we're launching an update to our family-formation supports (IVF, adoption, surrogacy, and foster-to-adopt). Details below and a short FAQ. :sparkles:
Priya (People Ops): TL;DR: up to 8 weeks paid leave for qualifying family-formation events, a $7,500 reimbursement pool for associated medical/legal costs, and dedicated case support from People Ops. Effective June 1.
Ethan (Eng): awesome, thanks — does this apply to all full-time headcount globally?
Leah (People Ops): Great q — policy applies to full-time employees in regions where we operate (US, CA, UK, EU). For APAC and other regions we'll provide local guidance and equivalent support where legal/benefit frameworks differ. Reach out if your country is missing.
Marco (People Ops): How to request: submit a confidential case via the HR Portal (link: https://redwood.hub/ff-support) or email people-ops@redwood.com. We’ll handle medical documentation securely and can coordinate leave dates with managers.
Ethan (Eng): Will managers see private medical docs?
Leah (People Ops): No — manager gets only leave timing and general accommodation notes. Medical documents are stored in the secure HR system and accessed by People Ops/Benefits only.
Maya (People Ops): Coverage highlights: 8 weeks paid leave for qualifying procedures/placements (can be continuous or intermittent over 12 months), plus up to $7,500 lifetime reimbursement per employee for treatment, legal, and travel costs. If you need more time, FMLA/LOA options still apply where eligible.
Priya (People Ops): We also added a flexible scheduling pilot for the 6 months after placement/procedure — reduced hours or phased return without needing to use PTO. Talk to your manager and People Ops to set this up.
Ethan (Eng): Is there a confidentiality option for teams that are small and where timing might give away info?
Leah (People Ops): Yes — you can request an anonymous notification template. People Ops will send a short team notice on your behalf (example: "Please welcome back Alex — they’ll be on a phased return starting next Monday.").
hr-bot: Reminder: policy doc uploaded to People Ops library — https://redwood.hub/ff-policy (pinned).
Marco (People Ops): Manager guidance: we’ve posted conversation scripts and accommodation checklists in the manager playbook. Please be supportive, avoid probing medical details, and escalate any disputes to People Ops.
Ethan (Eng): Any tax implications for the reimbursement?
Priya (People Ops): Good point — reimbursements may be taxable depending on jurisdiction. We include a short tax summary on the policy page and will run payroll with the right coding. Benefits team can follow up 1:1.
Maya (People Ops): FAQ highlights: 1) Eligibility window: active employees at the time of event. 2) Documentation: treatment/placement confirmation. 3) Retroactive requests: we can consider reimbursements for eligible events back to Jan 1 this year — file within 90 days.
Ethan (Eng): Appreciate the retro window. Is adoption legal support included?
Marco (People Ops): Yes — legal fees for adoption are eligible under the reimbursement pool, subject to receipts and policy limits.
Priya (People Ops): Next steps: read the short policy, use the request form if you need support, or DM People Ops for private questions. We’ll be holding office hours Friday 10–11am PT in #people-ops-help.
Leah (People Ops): For managers: join our 30-min drop-in on Monday 2pm PT for scenario Q&A.
Ethan (Eng): Thanks team. Really meaningful update. :heart:
Maya (People Ops): Thanks all — we know this is important and will iterate based on feedback. If you want to talk privately, ping me or Priya.
